newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks score record close,take cue from Wall St.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks score record close,take cue from Wall St.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng index scored a record close on Monday, taking its cue from Wall Street stocks which shattered more records on Friday and buoyed by continued bullish sentiment in the property market.
The index closed 122.60 points higher at 13,239.39, after setting a record intra-day high at 13,261.25. Turnover was HK$10.55 billion compared with HK$10.46 billion on Friday.
"Obviously it is on the back of New York on Friday," said Miles Remington, sales trader at Crosby Securities.
"Property is still the main word in Hong Kong's stock market at the moment," he added.
The Dow industrials closed 53.29 points higher at 6,471.76 on Friday, their 42nd record closing high for 1996.

Howard Gorges, director at South China Brokerage, said Hysan Development's acquisition of the Entertainment Building in Hong Kong's Central district for a rich price had allowed the recent market rally to broaden out to property investment companies.
"It has been another stimulus for the market," he said.
Hysan shares, which fell HK$0.75 on Friday following news of the deal, rose HK$1.15 to close at HK$29.30.
Great Eagle Holdings rose HK$1.30 to HK$32.30 and Amoy Properties added HK$0.50 to HK$11.60.
"A revaluation of property within Central is certainly boosting some of the stocks," said Remington.
Gorges also noted a strong tone in banking stocks.
HSBC Holdings rose HK$2.50 to HK$158.00 and Hang Seng Bank advanced HK$0.25 to HK$91.25.
"I think the banks could return to favour. They were leading the market up, then they went into quite heavy profit-taking. It looks like they have stabilised," said Gorges.
He said the rotation from one sector to another may prevent a large correction in the Hong Kong market.

"I would imagine that we can't go up in a straight line. Pretty soon I would expect the market to consolidate a bit but the undertone of the market through the last 10 days has been very strong so I don't think one can bet on a big correction," Gorges said.
But Remington said the 13,200-point area on the Hang Seng index seemed to be towards the top of the trading range in the short term.
Shares in Shanghai Industrial jumped HK$1.65 to HK$22.85 following news that the company would acquire various automotive, infrastructure, food and commercial interests.
